newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - spot supply woes continue.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - spot supply woes continue.

text.p: The New York physical coffee market was thinly traded this week, with shrinking levels of consumer stocks keeping spot differentials sky-high, traders said.
Traders said a decline in futures prices this week failed to spark offtake, as roasters seemed content to hang on and wait for the CSCE spot December contract to go off the board.
"It's slow because there is nothing to buy, and slow because roasters do not want to buy," a trader said. "Roasters are postponing buying and living off what they have."
While more coffee began to trickle into the market, traders said it was not enough to ease supply concerns -- or build stockpiles.
"Exports are getting snapped up by roasters as soon as they get here," one trader said. "Everyone is clamouring for coffee. It is extremely tight."

Underscoring the crunch, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported Friday supplies of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses fell in October by 351,000 60-kg bags, to 1,260,000 bags, their lowest level since the GCA began tracking inventories in January 1980.
